evidence.why: Shows the teardown guards and order.

facts.rationale: Distinguishes unconditional dispatch from optional callback execution and preserves the explicit local guards without asserting unverified registry semantics.
facts.value: After its validity assertion, Item_8026A8EC performs common cleanup and effect destruction, conditionally dispatches destruction presentation, and reaches the destroyed-hook dispatcher on every continuing path; the destroyed callback is invoked only if non-null. Fighter-owner detachment is guarded by x13, a non-null owner, and ftLib_80086960. The owner is then cleared. Camera cleanup requires its flag and pointer, each configured dynamics descriptor is passed to lb_8000FD18, and final cleanup, queued-effect clearing, and GObj unlinking follow.

facts.rationale: Preserves the proven ordering while correcting the implication that the callback executes unconditionally.
facts.value: Executes an ordered synchronous sequence: it_80273168 receives the item first; it_802742F4 receives the item, owner, and part second; RunGObjCallback invokes picked_up only when that slot is non-null; Item_8026B074 receives the Item record last. The outer function has no conditional branches, but the callback invocation is null-guarded.

evidence.why: Velocity copying/scaling and separately derived position.

facts.rationale: Direct helper inspection corrects the baseline's position-vector interpretation without changing the observed wrapper sequence.
facts.value: Receives an Item GObj, a release-velocity vector, and an f32 scalar. Stores the scalar verbatim in Item.xC44, calls it_802731A4, and forwards the vector to it_80273B50, which copies it into x40_vel and applies the item's throw-speed multiplier while deriving release position from the owner attachment. The wrapper dispatches dropped, calls it_80274198(gobj, true) and it_802754D4, then conditionally calls it_80275390 when it_8026B6C8 accepts the item.

The forwarded vector is copied into velocity and scaled.

facts.rationale: Preserves the exact C-level types while distinguishing canonical parameter spelling from the vector role proven by its consumer.
facts.value: Side-effect-only drop transition with semantic signature void(Item_GObj* gobj, Vec3* release_velocity, f32 drop_param). The canonical definition names the vector parameter pos, but its callee consumes it as velocity. Requires valid Item user data and a valid logic-table pointer; stores the scalar in Item.xC44 and returns no result. The wrapper does not guard the object or logic-table pointer.

evidence.why: Direct classification, increment/decrement, and capacity-check implementations.
Establishes cleanup ordering and shared transition-before-callback ordering.

facts.rationale: Preserves the supported shared lifecycle description while explicitly correcting the counter asymmetry and side-effecting category-9 limit check.
facts.value: ItemKind classification assigns hold_kind values 0 through 12. Creation bookkeeping increments the selected category counter except for hold_kind 9; category 0 additionally increments x1C when kind is It_Kind_M_Ball. Destruction decrements the counter selected by hold_kind, including x1C for category 9. Capacity checks cover selected categories, generally using >=; category 9 instead tests x1C > x20 and decrements x1C when returning true. Common destruction performs category bookkeeping before retained-resource cleanup. Pickup and drop paths call shared transition helpers before dispatching picked_up or dropped callbacks.
